title: The reconciled requirements
description: workareas/<workarea>/distil/requirements.json: what the programme must do, reconciled across every source's working set (held claims plus missed claims), written by the reconcile agent. On a re-distil, every existing id is kept. `tim distil coverage` validates it against this file, and also checks what a schema cannot: ids are unique, every cited claim is in the working set, every cited conflict is in conflicts.json, a question requirement cites a question conflict, an adopted change or exists requirement says how in `deltaNote`, only an adopted requirement carries `blockedBy`, every source with held claims backs at least one requirement or conflict, and, once backlog.json exists, every adopted requirement that is not `exists` sits in exactly one increment, one with `blockedBy` never in a todo one.

text.description: Text that is not empty or only whitespace.

requirement.description: One requirement: what must be true, why, and the claims that back it. Claims from different sources that say the same thing merge into one requirement that cites them all.

id.description: `req-NNN`. Stable: never renumber, because increments, the report and rulings cite it.

statement.description: What must be true, as something a user, operator or other system can observe.

why.description: Why it matters. For an out-of-scope requirement, why the goal excludes it.

claims.description: The claim ids that back it, from the working set: held extract claims and missed claims. Never a refuted claim. An adopted or question requirement never rests on a claim a precedence conflict overruled: the conflict records it instead.

status.description: adopted: it will be built (or is already met). question: it waits on an open question, and its conflict carries the default that will be built. out-of-scope: the goal excludes it.

delta.description: Against what the target repos do today: new (not there), change (there but different) or exists (already true, so it goes in the report and never in an increment).

deltaNote.description: For change: how today's behaviour differs. For exists: the target claim that already meets it. May be empty for new.

conflicts.description: The conflict ids from conflicts.json that touch it. [] when none does.

blockedBy.description: Adopted requirements only: who must do what outside the programme before it can be built, such as a platform change or access ("CDP raises the ingress request-body cap to at least 50MB (EUDPA-518)"). Never a design choice: that is a question. It sits in a blocked increment whose open questions name the blocker, never in a todo one.

then.description: An adopted change says how today differs, and an adopted exists names what already meets it.
